Independent enumeration of the 21 unordered support pairs and cubic bisection
correctness.rationale: Independent enumeration of unordered two-sums yields 15 fibers, six with two representations: three corner-pair versus doubled-midpoint fibers and three corner-plus-opposite-midpoint versus midpoint-pair fibers. Their extra terms have coefficients 4 and 8 respectively, on top of 2T² minus the sum of fourth powers. Completing squares gives the stated two-mass bound; Cauchy–Schwarz and AM–GM attain it at uniform positive magnitudes within each orbit, and equality for positive masses forces those magnitudes. The pure-orbit boundary is strictly suboptimal. The derivative in the ratio variable has exactly the stated cubic factor, with a single positive root; numerical substitution agrees with the printed values. At the optimum three necessary phase comparisons fix the affine-character form, which is also sufficient in every fiber. Modulo m,n ≥5 all two-sum fibers remain distinct; at (4,4) positive extremizing coefficients give a strict surplus from the (0,0), (4,0), (0,4) collision.
residual_risks: The grid conclusion concerns the specified nonaliasing rectangles and the sharp square cutoff, not every smaller rectangle. Numerical checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: This is the first quadratic simplex in two variables, a natural small test of exact Fourier synthesis bounds. The orbitwise equalization is not a consequence of symmetry alone; the result identifies the nonflat magnitudes that actually win over the phase-only optimum, and resolves all equality cases and the sharp square sampling cutoff.
residual_risks: The value is an exact six-mode benchmark, not a higher-degree theorem or a general grid-cutoff classification.
